newsitem.title: CHINA: Shanghai T-bill repo rates end down, spots up.
newsitem.headline: Shanghai T-bill repo rates end down, spots up.

text.p: Contracts on the treasury bill repurchase market in Shanghai closed mostly down on Wednesday ahead of a four-day break starting Thursday due to the Labour Day holiday and weekend, traders said.

The market and stock markets will be closed from Thursday to Sunday, removing a few days of use from the early-maturing contracts and making most traders reluctant to build positions on Wednesday, traders said.
"The holiday made most institutions reluctant to borrow on the repo market today," one trader said.
The annual rate for the most actively traded seven-day contract fell to 8.38 percent from 9.00 percent on Tuesday.
Total turnover of the six-contract market fell to 5.2 million lots from 5.7 million.
One lot is 1,000 yuan face value of treasury bills.
Traders said they expected the rates to rise on a technical rebound early next week after falls in the past two days.
Contracts on the T-bill spot market in Shanghai ended up across the board on Wednesday due to high yields, traders said.
The most actively traded 10-year bond that matures in June 2006 rose to 120.70 yuan from 119.66 yuan.
Combined volume of the seven-contract market fell to 1.1 million lots from 1.2 million lots.

Traders said the average yields of existing contracts are much higher the 9.18 annual coupon for the latest state debt issue, which will start on Thursday, leading to active buying on the market on Wednesday.
The spot prices are likely to fall slightly on a correction after the market re-open next Monday due to sharp gains this week, traders said.
